page_title: Dusty: free open-source CleanMyMac alternative for macOS

sources.entry: Dusty - Open-source menu bar disk cleaner that deletes only from a fixed allowlist, shows every path before removing it, and can undo a clean. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/yagcioglutoprak/dusty) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Dusty
summary.one_liner: Dusty is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed macOS menu bar disk cleaner that deletes only from a fixed allowlist of known safe targets and shows every path and size before removing anything.
use_cases: Reclaim disk space taken by Xcode DerivedData and simulators
Clear package-manager caches for npm, pip, Cargo, Go and others
Remove old node_modules, Cargo target dirs and virtualenvs in stale projects
Delete old .dmg and .pkg installers from Downloads
Safely preview cleanup sizes before deleting on a Mac
Replace a paid or closed-source Mac cleaner
summary.what_it_does: Dusty runs in the macOS menu bar and cleans three levels of targets: everyday items such as user caches, app logs, the Trash and browser caches; developer items such as Xcode DerivedData, unavailable simulators and package-manager caches (npm, yarn, pnpm, pip, uv, Cargo, Go, Homebrew, Gradle, CocoaPods and more); and look-before-you-leap items such as old installers, Xcode archives, local Time Machine snapshots, aged logs, opt-in Ollama models and stale project artifacts. A path can be deleted only if it descends from an explicit registry target, and protected folders like Documents, Desktop, Photos, Mail, iCloud Drive and Keychains are rejected. A dry-run mode reports exact bytes without removing anything, and Developer and Deep cleanups can move items to the Trash with an undo window. Every action is appended to a local JSON log, and a CLI and Shortcuts automation are offered.
notable: Allowlist-only deletion: cleanup targets are data in a public registry, and symlinks are never followed
Dry-run mode and per-path sizes shown before any deletion
Undo window via Trash for Developer and Deep cleanups, plus a local JSON action log
MIT licensed, no account or telemetry, installs via Homebrew cask
caveats: Some paths require Full Disk Access on macOS
Not an antivirus, app updater, duplicate finder or privacy scanner
Never runs as root and does not use sudo, which limits what it can touch
